campaign_run_disclosure.artefacts_produced_but_not_shipped_note: THESE FOUR PATHS DO NOT RESOLVE, BY DESIGN. They are the names the campaign's run would have written, listed so a reader knows what is missing — they are NOT citations and nothing in this deliverable is at them. campaign_run_disclosure.why_the_same_names_appear_in_all_three_s: they are a deterministic function of the design top, not a copied string: formal_harness_gen emits `formal_<top>.sv` with module `formal_<top>`, and formal_property_run writes `<module>_formal.sby` plus `<stem>.sby.log`. For top `spm` that is `formal_spm_formal.sby` in EVERY campaign of this design. Three independent campaign directories (one per PDK) each produced files with those names, and Phase-2 formal is PDK-invariant, so three identical reports are the expected outcome of three real runs — not evidence that one report was copied.
campaign_run_disclosure.why_they_were_not_shipped: the transcript `formal_spm_formal.sby.log` matches `.gitignore` rule `*.log`; the repo's un-ignore for evidence is `!benchmark-data/**/reports/**/*.log`, which rescues logs under a `reports/` directory only. A formal transcript lives under `phase2/stage1/formal/`, outside that rescue, so committing it requires an explicit `git add -f`. The `.sby` itself is not ignored — it was simply never copied when this deliverable was assembled (commit 1bea1377d published `reports/` and `phase2/stage1/rtl/`, and no `phase2/stage1/formal/` for any cell).
